meta.series: DSA for Freshers: Mid-level Company Roadmap
meta.batch: Part 4 (final batch of Level 2): Sorting + comparators, Greedy basics, Revision sheet
meta.note: company_tags indicative hain (frequently asked trends), official guarantee nahi. Intervals (merge/insert/min rooms) aur advanced greedy Level 3 me hain.

theory.concept: std::sort ko lambda comparator do to apni marzi ke order me sort hota hai. Comparator true tab return karta hai jab pehla element dusre se PEHLE aana chahiye. Ye strict weak ordering follow kare: irreflexive (comp(a, a) = false), asymmetric, transitive. Warna undefined behaviour ya crash.
key_points: Multi-key sorting: pehle primary key compare karo, equal ho to secondary: if(fx != fy) return fx < fy; return x > y;
Largest Number trick: a aur b ka order a+b > b+a (strings concatenate karke compare), ye valid strict weak ordering hai
pair / array / tuple default lexicographic sort hote hain (pehle first, phir second)
stable_sort equal elements ka relative order preserve karta hai
Comparator me <= kabhi mat use karo (comp(a, a) true ho jata hai, crash ho sakta hai)
Sorting ke dauraan comparator me container ko modify ya wahi container padhna (jise sort kar rahe ho) avoid karo; copy ya frequency map use karo
pitfalls: Comparator ke andar expensive kaam (count() har baar) O(n^2 log n) bana deta hai

theory.concept: Jab values ki range chhoti ho (e.g., 0..1000, a..z, heights 1..100), to comparison sort (O(n log n)) ki jagah frequency array se O(n + range) me sort ho jata hai. Frequency-based sorting (character frequency, H-Index) me bhi buckets kaam aate hain.
key_points: cnt[v]++ phir v ko ascending traverse karke cnt[v] baar output karo
Relative Sort Array / Custom Sort String: pehle given order ke elements, phir bacha hua
H-Index: bucket[min(citation, n)] banao, peeche se cumulative count dekho
Height Checker: counting sort se expected array on-the-fly milta hai (extra array ki zaroorat nahi)
pitfalls: Range bahut badi (1e9) ho to counting sort lagu nahi
Negative values ke liye offset zaroori
Stable counting sort ke liye prefix sums chahiye (yahan sirf values)

theory.concept: Kth element ke liye poori sorting zaroori nahi. Quicksort ka partition step kar do: pivot ka final index i mil jata hai. i == target index to done, warna sirf ek side me recurse. Average O(n), worst O(n^2) (random pivot se rare).
key_points: Kth largest = (n - k)-th smallest (0-indexed)
Random pivot se sorted input par bhi average O(n)
Bahut saare duplicates ho to 3-way partition use karo (Dutch National Flag)
Alternatives: sort O(n log n), min-heap of size k O(n log k) (Level 3), nth_element STL O(n)
pitfalls: Pivot hamesha last/first lena (sorted input par O(n^2))
Equal elements par infinite loop ya O(n^2)

theory.concept: Sorting ke baad kai problems local ho jati hain: minimum difference sirf adjacent elements me hota hai, overlap check sirf adjacent intervals me, triangle ke liye sabse bade teen elements. Isliye pehla step 'sort karo' hona chahiye jab order se matlab na ho.
key_points: Min absolute difference: sort karke adjacent diff
Meeting rooms (overlap): start se sort, har meeting ka start pichhle ke end se chhota to overlap
Intersection of arrays: dono sort, do pointers (multiset intersection)
Largest perimeter triangle: descending sort, pehla (a[i] < a[i+1] + a[i+2]) triplet
Sort karne se original index/order kho jata hai (agar zaroori ho to pair me index rakho)
pitfalls: Sort ke baad original positions chahiye ho
Interval overlap me <= vs < (end == start allowed?)

theory.concept: Greedy me har step par abhi ka sabse accha local choice liya jata hai aur kabhi wapas nahi badla jata. Ye tabhi sahi hai jab proof ho ki local choice kabhi global optimum se door nahi le jata. Proof ke do common tareeke: exchange argument (optimal solution me apna choice swap karke kharab nahi hota) aur 'greedy stays ahead'.
key_points: Pehle sort karna aksar greedy ka pehla step hota hai (cookies, boats, units on truck, two-city scheduling by difference)
Jab greedy fail hota hai: 0/1 knapsack, coin change (arbitrary coins) jaise problems me DP chahiye
Counterexample dhundo pehle: chhote input par brute force se compare karo (stress test)
Reachability greedy: farthest reachable index maintain karo (Jump Game)
Reset greedy: running total negative hote hi start aage badhao (Gas Station, Kadane)
Two-pass greedy: left se constraint, phir right se constraint (Candy)
Interval-type greedy (earliest end time first) Level 3 me aayegi
pitfalls: Ties break karne ka rule galat
Local choice ko baad me badalne ki zaroorat (tab DP)

problems.title: Sort Array by Increasing Frequency
problems.problem_statement: Sort the array in increasing order of frequency. If multiple values have the same frequency, sort them in decreasing order of value.
problems.description: Do-level sorting rule: pehle frequency (asc), tie par value (desc).
problems.theory: Frequency map banao, phir comparator: if(f[x] != f[y]) return f[x] < f[y]; return x > y;

brute_force.approach: Comparator ke andar har baar count() se frequency nikalo.
brute_force.code_cpp: vector<int> frequencySort(vector<int> a){ vector<int> b = a; sort(a.begin(), a.end(), [&](int x, int y){ int fx = count(b.begin(), b.end(), x), fy = count(b.begin(), b.end(), y); if(fx != fy) return fx < fy; return x > y; }); return a; }

optimized.approach: Frequency map ek baar, phir sort.
optimized.code_cpp: vector<int> frequencySort(vector<int> a){ unordered_map<int,int> f; for(int x : a) f[x]++; sort(a.begin(), a.end(), [&](int x, int y){ if(f[x] != f[y]) return f[x] < f[y]; return x > y; }); return a; }

problems.explanation: Brute me comparator ke andar O(n) kaam hone se total O(n^2 log n) ho gaya. Heavy computation ko comparator se bahar nikalo (precompute).

problems.title: Sort Characters By Frequency
problems.problem_statement: Sort the characters of a string in decreasing order of frequency (equal characters stay together). For determinism, characters with equal frequency are ordered by ASCII value ascending.
problems.description: LeetCode me equal frequency wale kisi bhi order me ho sakte hain; yahan test karne ke liye ascending char fix kiya hai.

test_cases.explanation: e freq 2, phir r aur t

problems.theory: freq[256] banao, characters ko (freq desc, char asc) se sort karo, phir har char ko freq baar likho.

brute_force.approach: Characters ko comparator me count() se sort.
brute_force.code_cpp: string frequencySortStr(string s){ string b = s; sort(s.begin(), s.end(), [&](char x, char y){ int fx = count(b.begin(), b.end(), x), fy = count(b.begin(), b.end(), y); if(fx != fy) return fx > fy; return x < y; }); return s; }

optimized.approach: Frequency array + sort distinct chars + build.
optimized.code_cpp: string frequencySortStr(const string& s){ int f[256] = {0}; for(unsigned char c : s) f[c]++; vector<int> ch; for(int c = 0; c < 256; c++) if(f[c]) ch.push_back(c); sort(ch.begin(), ch.end(), [&](int x, int y){ if(f[x] != f[y]) return f[x] > f[y]; return x < y; }); string r; for(int c : ch) r.append(f[c], (char)c); return r; }

problems.explanation: Poori string sort karne ki jagah sirf distinct characters (max 256) sort hote hain. Total O(n) jaisa. Heap/bucket sort se bhi hota hai.

problems.title: Largest Number
problems.problem_statement: Given non-negative integers, arrange them so they form the largest number and return it as a string.
problems.description: Result bahut bada ho sakta hai, isliye string return karo.
problems.theory: Do numbers x, y ka order: x pehle agar string(x)+string(y) > string(y)+string(x). Is comparator se sort karo. Sab zero ho to '0'.

brute_force.approach: Saari permutations try karo (chhote n ke liye), sabse bada string lo.
brute_force.code_cpp: string largestNumber(const vector<int>& a){ vector<string> s; for(int x : a) s.push_back(to_string(x)); sort(s.begin(), s.end()); string best = ""; do{ string c; for(auto& t : s) c += t; if(c.size() > best.size() || (c.size() == best.size() && c > best)) best = c; } while(next_permutation(s.begin(), s.end())); if(best[0] == '0') return "0"; return best; }

optimized.code_cpp: string largestNumber(const vector<int>& a){ vector<string> s; for(int x : a) s.push_back(to_string(x)); sort(s.begin(), s.end(), [](const string& x, const string& y){ return x + y > y + x; }); if(s[0] == "0") return "0"; string r; for(auto& t : s) r += t; return r; }

problems.explanation: Normal string compare ('3' vs '30') galat hai kyunki '30' > '3' par '330' > '303'. Concatenation compare isliye sahi hai ki wo directly final answer ko compare karta hai. Ye transitive hai (proof by exchange argument).

problems.title: Relative Sort Array
problems.problem_statement: Given arr1 and arr2 (distinct values, all in arr1), sort arr1 so elements appear in the same relative order as arr2. Elements not in arr2 go at the end in ascending order.
problems.description: arr2 ke elements ke saare duplicates ek saath aate hain.
constraints: arr2 distinct, each arr2 element is in arr1

test_cases.explanation: Pehle b ke order me, phir 7, 19

problems.theory: Counting array (value <= 1000). arr2 ke order me cnt[x] baar likho, phir 0..1000 ascending bache hue.

brute_force.approach: arr2 ke har element ke liye arr1 scan karke match nikalo, bache hue sort.
brute_force.code_cpp: vector<int> relativeSortArray(const vector<int>& a, const vector<int>& b){ vector<int> r; vector<bool> used(a.size(), false); for(int x : b) for(size_t i = 0; i < a.size(); i++) if(!used[i] && a[i] == x){ r.push_back(x); used[i] = true; } vector<int> rest; for(size_t i = 0; i < a.size(); i++) if(!used[i]) rest.push_back(a[i]); sort(rest.begin(), rest.end()); r.insert(r.end(), rest.begin(), rest.end()); return r; }

optimized.code_cpp: vector<int> relativeSortArray(const vector<int>& a, const vector<int>& b){ vector<int> cnt(1001, 0); for(int x : a) cnt[x]++; vector<int> r; for(int x : b){ while(cnt[x] > 0){ r.push_back(x); cnt[x]--; } } for(int v = 0; v <= 1000; v++) while(cnt[v] > 0){ r.push_back(v); cnt[v]--; } return r; }

problems.explanation: Value range chhoti hai (<= 1000) isliye counting sort best. Alternative: arr2 ka position map banake custom comparator.

problems.title: Sort Integers by The Number of 1 Bits
problems.problem_statement: Sort integers by the number of 1 bits in their binary representation (ascending). If two numbers have the same count, sort by value ascending.
problems.description: Two-key sort: popcount, phir value.
problems.theory: Comparator: popcount compare, tie par value. __builtin_popcount ya Kernighan loop.

brute_force.approach: Insertion sort (O(n^2)) with popcount key.
brute_force.code_cpp: vector<int> sortByBits(vector<int> a){ auto key = [](int x){ int c = 0; for(int t = x; t; t &= t - 1) c++; return c; }; for(size_t i = 1; i < a.size(); i++){ int v = a[i]; size_t j = i; while(j > 0 && (key(a[j-1]) > key(v) || (key(a[j-1]) == key(v) && a[j-1] > v))){ a[j] = a[j-1]; j--; } a[j] = v; } return a; }

optimized.code_cpp: vector<int> sortByBits(vector<int> a){ sort(a.begin(), a.end(), [](int x, int y){ int bx = __builtin_popcount(x), by = __builtin_popcount(y); if(bx != by) return bx < by; return x < y; }); return a; }

problems.explanation: Ye Level 1 ke 'Number of 1 Bits' aur sorting ka combination hai. Alternative trick: key = popcount * 100000 + value ek hi integer me.

problems.title: Custom Sort String
problems.problem_statement: Given a string order (unique characters) and a string s, permute s so characters appear in the order defined by 'order'. Characters of s not present in order go at the end (here: in ascending order, for determinism).
problems.description: order me jo characters pehle aate hain, s me bhi pehle aane chahiye.

test_cases.explanation: c, b, a ke baad d

problems.theory: s ki frequency array. order ke har character ko cnt baar likho (aur cnt = 0 karo), phir bache hue characters ascending.

brute_force.approach: order ke har character ke liye s scan, bache hue sort.
brute_force.code_cpp: string customSort(const string& order, const string& s){ string r, rest; vector<bool> used(s.size(), false); for(char o : order) for(size_t i = 0; i < s.size(); i++) if(!used[i] && s[i] == o){ r += s[i]; used[i] = true; } for(size_t i = 0; i < s.size(); i++) if(!used[i]) rest += s[i]; sort(rest.begin(), rest.end()); return r + rest; }

optimized.code_cpp: string customSort(const string& order, const string& s){ int cnt[256] = {0}; for(unsigned char c : s) cnt[c]++; string r; for(unsigned char c : order){ r.append(cnt[c], (char)c); cnt[c] = 0; } for(int c = 0; c < 256; c++) r.append(cnt[c], (char)c); return r; }

problems.explanation: Relative Sort Array ka string version. order ke character ko ek baar likhne ke baad cnt = 0 karna zaroori hai taaki aakhri loop me dobara na aaye.
edge_cases: order has chars absent in s

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problems.problem_statement: Given an integer array and k, return the k-th largest element (in sorted order, not distinct).
problems.description: Sort kiye bina average O(n) me solve karna interview ka follow-up hota hai.
problems.theory: Quickselect: kth largest = (n - k)-th smallest. Random pivot se partition karo aur sirf us side me jao jahan target index hai.

brute_force.approach: Poora array descending sort, a[k-1].
brute_force.code_cpp: int findKthLargest(vector<int> a, int k){ sort(a.begin(), a.end(), greater<int>()); return a[k - 1]; }

optimized.code_cpp:
int quickSelect(vector<int>& a, int l, int r, int k){ static mt19937 rng(12345); while(l < r){ int p = l + rng() % (r - l + 1); swap(a[p], a[r]); int pv = a[r], i = l; for(int j = l; j < r; j++) if(a[j] < pv) swap(a[i++], a[j]); swap(a[i], a[r]); if(i == k) return a[i]; if(i < k) l = i + 1; else r = i - 1; } return a[l]; }
int findKthLargest(vector<int> a, int k){ int n = a.size(); return quickSelect(a, 0, n - 1, n - k); }

problems.explanation: Har partition ke baad ek side discard ho jati hai: n + n/2 + n/4 + ... = O(n) expected. Min-heap of size k se O(n log k) hota hai (Level 3), nth_element STL me ready-made hai.

problems.title: Minimum Absolute Difference
problems.problem_statement: Given an array of distinct integers, find all pairs [a, b] (a < b) with the minimum absolute difference between any two elements. Return pairs in ascending order.
problems.description: Minimum difference sirf sorted order ke adjacent elements me hota hai.
problems.theory: Sort karo. Adjacent differences ka minimum nikalo, phir un adjacent pairs ko collect karo jinka diff minimum ho.

brute_force.approach: Saare pairs compare karo, minimum diff ke pairs collect + sort.
brute_force.code_cpp: vector<vector<int>> minimumAbsDifference(vector<int> a){ int n = a.size(), best = INT_MAX; for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) best = min(best, abs(a[i] - a[j])); vector<vector<int>> r; for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) if(abs(a[i] - a[j]) == best) r.push_back({min(a[i], a[j]), max(a[i], a[j])}); sort(r.begin(), r.end()); return r; }

optimized.code_cpp: vector<vector<int>> minimumAbsDifference(vector<int> a){ sort(a.begin(), a.end()); int best = INT_MAX; for(size_t i = 1; i < a.size(); i++) best = min(best, a[i] - a[i-1]); vector<vector<int>> r; for(size_t i = 1; i < a.size(); i++) if(a[i] - a[i-1] == best) r.push_back({a[i-1], a[i]}); return r; }

problems.explanation: Agar x aur z ke beech y aaye to |x - z| > |x - y|, isliye closest pair kabhi non-adjacent nahi hota (distinct elements ke liye). Duplicates hote to alag handling chahiye.

problems.title: Height Checker
problems.problem_statement: Students are standing in a line with given heights. The expected order is non-decreasing. Return the number of indices where the current height differs from the expected height.
problems.description: Expected = sorted version of heights.
problems.theory: Sorted copy se compare karo. Values 1..100 hain, isliye counting sort se extra array ke bina bhi expected value on-the-fly mil jati hai.

brute_force.approach: Copy banao, sort karo, compare.
brute_force.code_cpp: int heightChecker(const vector<int>& h){ vector<int> e = h; sort(e.begin(), e.end()); int c = 0; for(size_t i = 0; i < h.size(); i++) if(h[i] != e[i]) c++; return c; }

optimized.code_cpp: int heightChecker(const vector<int>& h){ int cnt[101] = {0}; for(int x : h) cnt[x]++; int c = 0, v = 1; for(size_t i = 0; i < h.size(); i++){ while(cnt[v] == 0) v++; if(h[i] != v) c++; cnt[v]--; } return c; }

problems.explanation: Small range hone ki wajah se O(n) possible. 'Expected array' ko explicitly banane ki bhi zaroorat nahi padti.

problems.title: Intersection of Two Arrays II
problems.problem_statement: Given two integer arrays, return their intersection. Each element appears as many times as it shows in both arrays. (Here the result is returned in ascending order for determinism.)
problems.description: Multiset intersection: duplicates ki ginti bhi count hoti hai.
problems.theory: Dono arrays sort karo, do pointers. Equal ho to result me daalo aur dono aage; warna chhota wala aage.

brute_force.approach: Har element ke liye dusre array me unused match dhundo.
brute_force.code_cpp: vector<int> intersect(const vector<int>& a, const vector<int>& b){ vector<bool> used(b.size(), false); vector<int> r; for(int x : a) for(size_t j = 0; j < b.size(); j++) if(!used[j] && b[j] == x){ used[j] = true; r.push_back(x); break; } sort(r.begin(), r.end()); return r; }

optimized.time: O(n log n + m log m)
optimized.code_cpp: vector<int> intersect(vector<int> a, vector<int> b){ sort(a.begin(), a.end()); sort(b.begin(), b.end()); size_t i = 0, j = 0; vector<int> r; while(i < a.size() && j < b.size()){ if(a[i] < b[j]) i++; else if(a[i] > b[j]) j++; else { r.push_back(a[i]); i++; j++; } } return r; }

problems.explanation: HashMap (frequency) se O(n + m) bhi hota hai. Arrays pehle se sorted ho to two pointers me sorting bhi nahi lagti (follow-up). Level 1 ka L1-015 unique intersection tha, ye multiset version hai.

problems.title: H-Index
problems.problem_statement: Given an array of citation counts for a researcher's papers, return the researcher's h-index: the maximum h such that the researcher has at least h papers with at least h citations each.
problems.description: Total n papers hain, isliye h <= n.
problems.theory: Bucket count: b[min(c, n)]++. Peeche se (h = n ... 0) cumulative total; total >= h hote hi answer h.

brute_force.approach: h = n se neeche, har h ke liye count(c >= h).
brute_force.code_cpp: int hIndex(const vector<int>& c){ int n = c.size(); for(int h = n; h >= 1; h--){ int cnt = 0; for(int x : c) if(x >= h) cnt++; if(cnt >= h) return h; } return 0; }

optimized.code_cpp: int hIndex(const vector<int>& c){ int n = c.size(); vector<int> b(n + 1, 0); for(int x : c) b[min(x, n)]++; int total = 0; for(int h = n; h >= 0; h--){ total += b[h]; if(total >= h) return h; } return 0; }

problems.explanation: Citations ko n par cap karte hain kyunki h kabhi n se bada nahi ho sakta. Sort karke (descending) bhi O(n log n) me ho jata hai: pehla index i jahan c[i] < i + 1.

problems.title: Meeting Rooms (Can Attend All)
problems.problem_statement: Given meeting time intervals [start, end), determine if a person can attend all meetings (no two meetings overlap). A meeting ending at time t and another starting at t do not overlap.
problems.description: Sirf overlap check karna hai, rooms ki ginti nahi (wo Level 3 me).
problems.theory: Start time se sort karo. Koi bhi adjacent pair me next.start < prev.end ho to overlap.

brute_force.approach: Saare pairs overlap check.
brute_force.code_cpp: bool canAttend(const vector<array<int,2>>& v){ int n = v.size(); for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) if(v[i][0] < v[j][1] && v[j][0] < v[i][1]) return false; return true; }

optimized.code_cpp: bool canAttend(vector<array<int,2>> v){ sort(v.begin(), v.end()); for(size_t i = 1; i < v.size(); i++) if(v[i][0] < v[i-1][1]) return false; return true; }

problems.explanation: Sort ke baad agar koi i, j (j > i+1) overlap karte hain to i aur i+1 bhi overlap karenge, isliye adjacent check kaafi hai. Intervals ka pura topic (merge, insert, min rooms) Level 3 me.

problems.title: Largest Perimeter Triangle
problems.problem_statement: Given an array of side lengths, return the largest perimeter of a triangle with non-zero area formed from three of these lengths. Return 0 if impossible.
problems.description: Triangle inequality: do chhoti sides ka sum badi side se bada hona chahiye.
problems.theory: Descending sort karo. Pehla triplet (a[i], a[i+1], a[i+2]) jahan a[i] < a[i+1] + a[i+2] sabse bada perimeter dega, kyunki baaki triplets chhote hain.

brute_force.approach: Saare triplets par triangle check.
brute_force.code_cpp: int largestPerimeter(const vector<int>& a){ int n = a.size(), best = 0; for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) for(int k = j + 1; k < n; k++){ int x = a[i], y = a[j], z = a[k]; if(x + y > z && x + z > y && y + z > x) best = max(best, x + y + z); } return best; }

optimized.code_cpp: int largestPerimeter(vector<int> a){ sort(a.begin(), a.end(), greater<int>()); for(size_t i = 0; i + 2 < a.size(); i++) if(a[i] < a[i+1] + a[i+2]) return a[i] + a[i+1] + a[i+2]; return 0; }

problems.explanation: Greedy argument: sabse bada side fix karke uske liye sabse bade do partners lo; agar wo bhi fail ho to koi aur partner kaam nahi karega. Valid Triangle Number (L2-044) ka greedy cousin.

problems.title: Assign Cookies
problems.problem_statement: Each child i has greed g[i] (minimum cookie size they accept); each cookie j has size s[j]. A child gets at most one cookie and a cookie goes to at most one child. Maximize the number of content children.
problems.description: Cookie size >= greed ho tabhi child content.
problems.theory: Dono sort karo. Sabse kam greedy wale bachche ko sabse chhoti sufficient cookie do. Two pointers: cookie child ke liye kaafi ho to child content, warna agli (bigger) cookie.

brute_force.approach: Sort children; har bachche ke liye sabse chhoti unused sufficient cookie scan karke.
brute_force.code_cpp: int findContentChildren(vector<int> g, vector<int> s){ sort(g.begin(), g.end()); sort(s.begin(), s.end()); vector<bool> used(s.size(), false); int c = 0; for(int x : g){ for(size_t j = 0; j < s.size(); j++) if(!used[j] && s[j] >= x){ used[j] = true; c++; break; } } return c; }

optimized.time: O(n log n + m log m)
optimized.code_cpp: int findContentChildren(vector<int> g, vector<int> s){ sort(g.begin(), g.end()); sort(s.begin(), s.end()); size_t i = 0; for(size_t j = 0; j < s.size() && i < g.size(); j++) if(s[j] >= g[i]) i++; return i; }

problems.explanation: Chhoti cookie bade greed wale ke kaam ki nahi, isliye usse sabse kam greed wale ko dena hi safe hai (exchange argument). Brute me har bar scan hota hai, optimized me ek hi pass.

problems.title: Lemonade Change
problems.problem_statement: Lemonade costs $5. Customers pay with $5, $10 or $20 bills one at a time in order. You start with no change. Return true if you can give correct change to every customer.
problems.description: $20 par change me $10 + $5 ya $5 + $5 + $5 do ho sakta hai.
problems.theory: Greedy: $20 par pehle $10 + $5 do (kyunki $5 zyada kaam ke hain, $10 sirf $20 ke change me use hota hai). Nahi to teen $5.

brute_force.approach: Backtracking: $20 par dono tareeke try karo.
brute_force.code_cpp:
bool rec(const vector<int>& b, int i, int c5, int c10){ if(i == (int)b.size()) return true; int x = b[i]; if(x == 5) return rec(b, i + 1, c5 + 1, c10); if(x == 10){ if(c5 == 0) return false; return rec(b, i + 1, c5 - 1, c10 + 1); } if(c10 > 0 && c5 > 0 && rec(b, i + 1, c5 - 1, c10 - 1)) return true; if(c5 >= 3 && rec(b, i + 1, c5 - 3, c10)) return true; return false; }
bool lemonadeChange(const vector<int>& b){ return rec(b, 0, 0, 0); }

optimized.code_cpp: bool lemonadeChange(const vector<int>& b){ int c5 = 0, c10 = 0; for(int x : b){ if(x == 5) c5++; else if(x == 10){ if(!c5) return false; c5--; c10++; } else { if(c10 && c5){ c10--; c5--; } else if(c5 >= 3) c5 -= 3; else return false; } } return true; }

problems.explanation: Backtracking me har $20 par do branch hote hain. Greedy proof: $10 sirf $20 ke change me kaam aate hain, jabki $5 har jagah, isliye $10 pehle kharch karo.

problems.title: Maximum Units on a Truck
problems.problem_statement: boxTypes[i] = [numberOfBoxes, unitsPerBox]. The truck can carry at most truckSize boxes. Return the maximum total number of units that can be put on the truck.
problems.description: Box type ke saare boxes lene zaroori nahi.
problems.theory: Jis box me zyada units, pehle usko lo: units per box descending sort, phir jitne boxes ja sakte hain uthao.

brute_force.approach: Ek-ek box uthao: har baar bache hue me se sabse zyada units wala type.
brute_force.code_cpp: int maximumUnits(vector<array<int,2>> b, int size){ int total = 0; while(size > 0){ int bi = -1; for(size_t i = 0; i < b.size(); i++) if(b[i][0] > 0 && (bi < 0 || b[i][1] > b[bi][1])) bi = i; if(bi < 0) break; b[bi][0]--; size--; total += b[bi][1]; } return total; }

optimized.approach: Sort by units desc + bulk take.
optimized.code_cpp: int maximumUnits(vector<array<int,2>> b, int size){ sort(b.begin(), b.end(), [](const array<int,2>& x, const array<int,2>& y){ return x[1] > y[1]; }); int total = 0; for(auto& t : b){ int take = min(t[0], size); total += take * t[1]; size -= take; if(!size) break; } return total; }

problems.explanation: Fractional knapsack jaisa hi greedy hai (value/weight = units per box, weight = 1 box). Brute me truckSize bada ho (1e6) to slow, isliye bulk take.

problems.title: Jump Game
problems.problem_statement: a[i] is the maximum jump length from index i. Starting at index 0, return true if you can reach the last index.
problems.description: Max jump hai, exact jump nahi.
problems.theory: Farthest reachable index maintain karo. Agar i > farthest to waha tak pahunch hi nahi sakte (false); warna farthest = max(farthest, i + a[i]).

brute_force.approach: DP: reachable[] array; har reachable index se aage ke saare indices mark.
brute_force.code_cpp: bool canJump(const vector<int>& a){ int n = a.size(); vector<bool> r(n, false); r[0] = true; for(int i = 0; i < n; i++){ if(!r[i]) continue; for(int j = 1; j <= a[i] && i + j < n; j++) r[i + j] = true; } return r[n - 1]; }

optimized.code_cpp: bool canJump(const vector<int>& a){ int far = 0; for(int i = 0; i < (int)a.size(); i++){ if(i > far) return false; far = max(far, i + a[i]); } return true; }

problems.explanation: Reachable set hamesha 0 se 'far' tak ek continuous range hoti hai, isliye poora reachable array banane ki zaroorat nahi.

problems.title: Jump Game II
problems.problem_statement: a[i] is the maximum jump length from index i. Return the minimum number of jumps to reach the last index. It is guaranteed you can reach it.
problems.description: Minimum jumps chahiye, sirf reachability nahi.
problems.theory: BFS-levels jaisa soch: current jump ki range (curEnd) aur uske andar se farthest reach. i == curEnd par jump count++ aur curEnd = farthest.

brute_force.approach: DP: dp[i] = i tak pahunchne ke min jumps; har index se aage relax.
brute_force.code_cpp: int jump(const vector<int>& a){ int n = a.size(); vector<int> dp(n, INT_MAX); dp[0] = 0; for(int i = 0; i < n; i++){ if(dp[i] == INT_MAX) continue; for(int j = 1; j <= a[i] && i + j < n; j++) dp[i + j] = min(dp[i + j], dp[i] + 1); } return dp[n - 1]; }

optimized.code_cpp: int jump(const vector<int>& a){ int n = a.size(), jumps = 0, curEnd = 0, far = 0; for(int i = 0; i < n - 1; i++){ far = max(far, i + a[i]); if(i == curEnd){ jumps++; curEnd = far; } } return jumps; }

problems.explanation: Har jump ek 'level' hai; us level ke saare indices me se jo sabse door pahunchta hai wahi agla level decide karta hai. Loop n-1 tak isliye ki last index par jump count nahi badhana.

problems.title: Gas Station
problems.problem_statement: There are n gas stations on a circular route; station i has gas[i] fuel and travelling to the next station costs cost[i]. Return the starting station index from which you can complete the circuit clockwise, or -1. If a solution exists it is unique.
problems.description: Tank khali se start hota hai, kisi bhi moment par tank negative nahi hona chahiye.
problems.theory: Agar total gas < total cost to -1. Warna running tank negative hote hi us point tak ka koi bhi start galat; start = i + 1, tank = 0. End me bacha hua start answer.

brute_force.approach: Har station se simulate karke circuit complete check.
brute_force.code_cpp: int canCompleteCircuit(const vector<int>& g, const vector<int>& c){ int n = g.size(); for(int s = 0; s < n; s++){ int tank = 0; bool ok = true; for(int k = 0; k < n; k++){ int i = (s + k) % n; tank += g[i] - c[i]; if(tank < 0){ ok = false; break; } } if(ok) return s; } return -1; }

optimized.approach: Single pass with total and tank reset.
optimized.code_cpp: int canCompleteCircuit(const vector<int>& g, const vector<int>& c){ int n = g.size(), total = 0, tank = 0, start = 0; for(int i = 0; i < n; i++){ int d = g[i] - c[i]; total += d; tank += d; if(tank < 0){ start = i + 1; tank = 0; } } return total >= 0 ? start : -1; }

problems.explanation: Proof sketch: agar start s se i par tank negative hua to s se i ke beech ka koi bhi station start nahi ban sakta (unse bhi i tak ka sum negative hi aata). Total >= 0 ho to last reset point hi valid start hai. Ye Kadane ke reset idea jaisa hai.

problems.title: Non-decreasing Array (At Most One Modification)
problems.problem_statement: Given an array, check if it can become non-decreasing by modifying at most one element (to any value).
problems.description: Modification ki value koi bhi ho sakti hai.
problems.theory: Pehla violation (a[i] < a[i-1]) milne par choose karo: a[i-1] ko chhota karo (a[i-1] = a[i]) ya a[i] ko bada (a[i] = a[i-1]). Agar a[i] < a[i-2] ho to a[i] ko bada karna padega, warna a[i-1] ko chhota. Dusra violation aaye to false.

brute_force.approach: Har index ko pados ki value se replace karke sorted check.
brute_force.code_cpp: bool checkPossibility(const vector<int>& a){ int n = a.size(); auto isSorted = [&](const vector<int>& v){ for(size_t i = 1; i < v.size(); i++) if(v[i] < v[i-1]) return false; return true; }; if(isSorted(a)) return true; for(int i = 0; i < n; i++){ vector<int> cand; if(i > 0) cand.push_back(a[i-1]); if(i + 1 < n) cand.push_back(a[i+1]); for(int v : cand){ vector<int> b = a; b[i] = v; if(isSorted(b)) return true; } } return false; }

optimized.approach: Single pass, fix at the first violation greedily.
optimized.code_cpp: bool checkPossibility(vector<int> a){ int cnt = 0; for(int i = 1; i < (int)a.size(); i++){ if(a[i] < a[i-1]){ if(++cnt > 1) return false; if(i >= 2 && a[i] < a[i-2]) a[i] = a[i-1]; else a[i-1] = a[i]; } } return true; }

problems.explanation: Greedy choice: jab bhi possible ho a[i-1] ko chhota karo (a[i] ko bada karne se aage ke liye rukawat ban sakti hai). Sirf a[i] < a[i-2] hone par a[i] ko bada karna padta hai.

problems.title: Partition Labels
problems.problem_statement: Partition a string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part. Return the sizes of the parts.
problems.description: Parts ko jodne par wahi string milti hai.
problems.theory: Har letter ka last index nikalo. Part ki end = us part me aaye letters ke last indices ka maximum. i == end par part complete.

brute_force.approach: Har part ke liye end ko rfind se baar baar badhao.
brute_force.code_cpp: vector<int> partitionLabels(const string& s){ int n = s.size(); vector<int> r; int i = 0; while(i < n){ int end = s.rfind(s[i]); int j = i; while(j <= end){ end = max(end, (int)s.rfind(s[j])); j++; } r.push_back(end - i + 1); i = end + 1; } return r; }

optimized.code_cpp: vector<int> partitionLabels(const string& s){ int last[26] = {0}; for(int i = 0; i < (int)s.size(); i++) last[s[i] - 'a'] = i; vector<int> r; int start = 0, end = 0; for(int i = 0; i < (int)s.size(); i++){ end = max(end, last[s[i] - 'a']); if(i == end){ r.push_back(end - start + 1); start = i + 1; } } return r; }

problems.explanation: Greedy: part ko jaldi se jaldi close karo (jis point par us part ke saare letters ka last occurrence cover ho jaye). Ye interval-merging ka hi ek disguised version hai.

problems.title: Two City Scheduling
problems.problem_statement: 2n people must be sent to city A or city B, exactly n to each. costs[i] = [aCost, bCost]. Return the minimum total cost.
problems.description: Exactly n log har city me jayenge.
problems.theory: Sabko pehle B bhejne ka socho. Fir n logon ko A bhejo jinke liye (aCost - bCost) sabse chhota (sabse zyada bachat). Matlab difference se sort karo, pehle n A me, baaki B me.

brute_force.approach: Saare C(2n, n) subsets try karo (bitmask).
brute_force.code_cpp: int twoCitySchedCost(const vector<array<int,2>>& c){ int m = c.size(), n = m / 2, best = INT_MAX; for(int mask = 0; mask < (1 << m); mask++){ if(__builtin_popcount(mask) != n) continue; int s = 0; for(int i = 0; i < m; i++) s += ((mask >> i) & 1) ? c[i][0] : c[i][1]; best = min(best, s); } return best; }

optimized.code_cpp: int twoCitySchedCost(vector<array<int,2>> c){ sort(c.begin(), c.end(), [](const array<int,2>& x, const array<int,2>& y){ return x[0] - x[1] < y[0] - y[1]; }); int n = c.size() / 2, s = 0; for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += c[i][0]; for(int i = n; i < 2 * n; i++) s += c[i][1]; return s; }

problems.explanation: (aCost - bCost) 'A ko prefer karne ki bachat' hai. Jinki bachat zyada hai unhe A bhejna sahi hai. Total = sum(b) + sum of chosen differences, isliye difference se sort karna hi optimal.

problems.title: Candy
problems.problem_statement: Children stand in a line with ratings. Each child must get at least one candy, and a child with a higher rating than a neighbour must get more candies than that neighbour. Return the minimum total candies.
problems.description: Dono neighbours (left aur right) ko dekhna padta hai.
problems.theory: Do passes: left to right (agar r[i] > r[i-1] to c[i] = c[i-1] + 1), phir right to left (agar r[i] > r[i+1] to c[i] = max(c[i], c[i+1] + 1)). Dono constraints alag-alag satisfy ho jaate hain.

brute_force.approach: Sabko 1 candy se shuru, jab tak koi rule violate ho fix karte raho.
brute_force.code_cpp: int candy(const vector<int>& r){ int n = r.size(); vector<int> c(n, 1); bool ch = true; while(ch){ ch = false; for(int i = 0; i < n; i++){ if(i > 0 && r[i] > r[i-1] && c[i] <= c[i-1]){ c[i] = c[i-1] + 1; ch = true; } if(i + 1 < n && r[i] > r[i+1] && c[i] <= c[i+1]){ c[i] = c[i+1] + 1; ch = true; } } } return accumulate(c.begin(), c.end(), 0); }

optimized.code_cpp: int candy(const vector<int>& r){ int n = r.size(); vector<int> c(n, 1); for(int i = 1; i < n; i++) if(r[i] > r[i-1]) c[i] = c[i-1] + 1; for(int i = n - 2; i >= 0; i--) if(r[i] > r[i+1]) c[i] = max(c[i], c[i+1] + 1); return accumulate(c.begin(), c.end(), 0); }

problems.explanation: Ek pass me dono sides ko handle karna mushkil hai; do alag passes me har side ka constraint satisfy hota hai aur max lene se dono. Equal ratings par koi constraint nahi (1 candy bhi chalegi).

problems.title: Task Scheduler
problems.problem_statement: Tasks are labeled A-Z; each takes one unit of time. The same task must have at least n units of cooldown between two runs. The CPU may be idle. Return the minimum number of units to finish all tasks.
problems.description: Order of tasks free hai, par cooldown rule follow karna hai.

test_cases.explanation: A B idle A B idle A B
A ke beech idle slots bharne ke liye kaafi tasks nahi

problems.theory: Sabse zyada frequency (mx) wala task frame banata hai: (mx - 1) frames of size (n + 1) plus last frame me wo tasks jinki freq mx hai (numMax). Answer = max(total tasks, (mx - 1) * (n + 1) + numMax).

brute_force.approach: Time-step simulation: har step par cooldown se bahar wale tasks me se sabse zyada bache wala chalao.
brute_force.code_cpp: int leastInterval(const string& t, int n){ int cnt[26] = {0}; for(char c : t) cnt[c - 'A']++; int last[26]; fill(last, last + 26, -1000000); int remaining = t.size(), time = 0; while(remaining > 0){ int pick = -1; for(int i = 0; i < 26; i++) if(cnt[i] > 0 && time - last[i] > n){ if(pick < 0 || cnt[i] > cnt[pick]) pick = i; } if(pick >= 0){ cnt[pick]--; last[pick] = time; remaining--; } time++; } return time; }

optimized.code_cpp: int leastInterval(const string& t, int n){ int cnt[26] = {0}; for(char c : t) cnt[c - 'A']++; int mx = *max_element(cnt, cnt + 26); int numMax = count(cnt, cnt + 26, mx); return max((int)t.size(), (mx - 1) * (n + 1) + numMax); }

problems.explanation: Idle slots sirf tab lagte hain jab dusre tasks se frames bhar nahi paate; agar bahut saare tasks hon to idle zero aur answer = total tasks. Ye max-heap + cooldown queue se bhi hota hai (Level 3).

problems.title: Increasing Triplet Subsequence
problems.problem_statement: Return true if there exist indices i < j < k with a[i] < a[j] < a[k]. Solve in O(n) time and O(1) space.
problems.description: Subsequence continuous nahi hona chahiye.
problems.theory: Do variables: first = sabse chhota ab tak, second = sabse chhota 'second element of a pair'. x <= first to first = x; x <= second to second = x; warna x teesra element hai => true.

brute_force.approach: Teen nested loops.
brute_force.code_cpp: bool increasingTriplet(const vector<int>& a){ int n = a.size(); for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) for(int k = j + 1; k < n; k++) if(a[i] < a[j] && a[j] < a[k]) return true; return false; }

optimized.code_cpp: bool increasingTriplet(const vector<int>& a){ long long f = LLONG_MAX, s = LLONG_MAX; for(int x : a){ if(x <= f) f = x; else if(x <= s) s = x; else return true; } return false; }

problems.explanation: second ke paas hamesha koi chhoti value hai jo uske pehle aayi thi (chahe first baad me update ho gaya ho), isliye teesra element milte hi triplet pakka hai. Ye LIS (Longest Increasing Subsequence) ke patience-sorting idea ka k = 3 case hai.

level_revision.title: Level 2 Revision Sheet (Part 1 to 4: L2-001 to L2-100)

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Window ki length k pehle se fixed (sum, average, vowel count, anagram, deque max)
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: Add a[i], remove a[i-k], answer update

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Longest/shortest subarray ya substring with a monotonic condition (non-negative / counts)
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: r expand; while condition invalid -> l++; best = max(best, r - l + 1)

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Exactly k type counts (odd numbers, distinct integers)
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: Exactly k = atMost(k) - atMost(k-1); count += r - l + 1

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Max/min subarray sum, product, circular, absolute sum
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: cur = max(a[i], cur + a[i]); best = max(best, cur)

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Bahut saare range sum queries, product except self
Bahut saare range updates, final array ek baar
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: d[l] += v, d[r+1] -= v, prefix sum

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Subarray with sum k / divisible by k / equal 0-1 / XOR k (negatives allowed)
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: Same prefix (ya prefix - k) pehle dikha? cnt[0] = 1 ya first[0] = -1 seed
Sort, fix outer elements, l/r pointers, skip duplicates

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Container/trapping water/boats: limiting side move karo
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: Chhoti side wale pointer ko hilao

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: First/last position, insert position, kth missing, wraparound
Rotated array, peak, single element, 2D flatten
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: Sorted half ya slope se half discard

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Minimize the maximum / maximize the minimum, least speed/capacity/days
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: Monotonic feasible(mid) greedy check, lo/hi on answer range

pattern_cheat_sheet.pattern: Binary search on value range + counting
pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Kth smallest in matrix, find duplicate, median partition
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: count(<= mid) se half decide karo
Strict weak ordering lambda; heavy work comparator se bahar
Random pivot partition, ek side discard

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Min difference, overlap, intersection, small range
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: Sort ke baad local compare ya counting sort

pattern_cheat_sheet.when_to_use: Reach, schedule, assign, partition, two-pass constraints
pattern_cheat_sheet.idea: Exchange argument / stays-ahead proof, stress test se verify

decision_guide: Subarray sum with negatives -> prefix sum + HashMap
Sorted array ya monotonic answer -> binary search (index ya answer)
'Minimize the maximum' / 'maximize the minimum' -> binary search on answer + greedy check
Pairs/triplets with target and order irrelevant -> sort + two pointers
Many range updates -> difference array; many range queries -> prefix sum
Ordering by rules -> comparator ya counting sort
Local choice provable -> greedy; warna DP (Level 5)

complexity_cheat_sheet.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) or O(charset) space
Usually O(n) or O(n log n) with sorting

common_mistakes: Sliding window ko negative numbers par lagana (prefix sum + HashMap chahiye)
Prefix + HashMap me cnt[0] = 1 seed bhoolna ya update ko query se pehle karna
Binary search me lo/hi/mid update galat (infinite loop): max-feasible search me upper mid use karo
Binary search on answer me range galat (lo = max element, hi = sum) ya feasible function monotonic na hona
Comparator me <= use karna ya inconsistent (non-transitive) rules
int overflow: sums/products ke liye long long, mid * mid, ceil division with long long
Greedy ko bina proof ya counterexample check ke lagana
Duplicates skip na karna (3Sum/4Sum) ya galat jagah par skip karna
kth largest vs kth smallest index confusion (n - k)
interview_checklist: 1. Constraints se complexity target nikalo (n <= 1e5 => O(n log n) ya O(n))
2. Brute force bolo aur bottleneck pehchano (repeated work? search? sort?)
3. Pattern pick karo (decision guide dekho) aur reason batao
4. Monotonicity / negatives / sorted hone jaisi assumptions explicitly bolo
5. Template se code likho, chhote example par dry run karo
6. Edge cases: empty, n = 1, all same, negatives, overflow, duplicates
7. Complexity bolo aur trade-offs (space vs time) batao
8. Agar sawaal me follow-up ho (O(1) space, no sort) to approach adjust karo

self_test_before_level_3.instruction: Bina solution dekhe, har problem ka brute + optimized approach aur complexity 10-12 minute me explain kar sako to Level 3 ke liye ready ho.
